items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns effective immediately amid spy-affair scandal; CFO Colette Kress interim CEO
items.summary: Nvidia announced Huang resigned as President, CEO and board member on Nov 12 following the Nov 9-10 reports of his relationship with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese intelligence asset, plus a separate affair with a company executive. CFO Colette Kress becomes interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones was named the company's first-ever independent board chair; Nvidia's market cap fell below $4T for the first time since July 2025.
items.actionable: A leadership vacuum at the company most central to the US-China chip-export fight raises the odds of a harder US export-policy line (Huang had been the industry's loudest China-access advocate) -- structurally bullish for SMIC (0981.HK) as the onshore foundry alternative, and a reason to keep the broader HK tech book (Tencent, Xiaomi) hedged against fresh chip-policy headline risk rather than adding into any bounce.

items.headline: China extends rare-earth export-control suspension to January 10, 2027 -- resolves the Nov 10 cliff-edge
items.summary: MOFCOM and China's customs authority published a notice on Nov 9 extending the October-2025 rare-earth/battery/graphite export-control suspension (including the 0.1%-content extraterritorial rule) for a further two months, from Nov 11, 2026 to Jan 10, 2027, just a day before the original pause was due to lapse. The April-2025 licensing requirements on seven medium/heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium, etc.) were not touched and remain in force.
items.actionable: Removes the near-term tail risk flagged on the rare-earth watchlist (no abrupt re-imposition of the broad 0.1% rule) -- modestly bearish for the urgency of MP Materials/Lynas re-shoring narratives in the next two months but reduces downside volatility risk into year-end; the new Jan 10, 2027 date is the next hard deadline to watch.

items.headline: Alibaba HK shares fall 6.8% (~$17.3B market-cap loss) as T-Head chip spin-off advances; Hang Seng closes -1.26%
items.summary: Alibaba shares closed at HK$93.80 on Nov 12, down 6.8% from HK$100.60, after confirming it is proceeding with a Hong Kong spin-off/IPO of its in-house AI-chip unit T-Head (an Nvidia rival) after winning an HKEX waiver on guaranteed shareholder allocation. The Hang Seng Index fell 307 points (-1.26%) to 24,008.55 on broad tech weakness, with Tencent down 2.6% to HK$398.80.
items.actionable: The T-Head spin-off is a structurally bullish, multi-quarter catalyst for China's domestic AI-chip ambitions (and by extension SMIC's foundry role) but the near-term HK tech tape is digesting both this overhang and the Nvidia CEO shock simultaneously -- expect continued volatility in the HK tech sleeve into SGX/HKEX's 09:00/09:30 SGT open rather than a clean read-through either way.

items.headline: Gold closes below $4,000-equivalent, silver and miners extend Fed-hike-driven rout into Thursday close
items.summary: GLD fell 2.8% to $354.89 and SLV fell 3.3% to $45.12 on Thursday, with GDX down 4.0% to $81.84 -- the second straight down session as the hawkish December-hike repricing (Waller's Nov 10 remarks plus hot CPI) continues to pressure precious metals and miners. This confirms Wednesday's intraday break below $4,000 spot gold/$52 spot silver carried through to an actual US-session close.
items.actionable: Two consecutive down closes (not just an intraday dip) confirms the gold/silver/miner leg of the book is in a genuine drawdown tied to the Dec FOMC repricing, not a one-session wobble -- the 1.6x levered silver position is the most exposed line item here and should be sized for further downside until the Dec 8-9 FOMC resolves the 50bp-hike tail risk.

items.headline: Bitcoin slides toward $71k, crypto Fear & Greed at 28 as Nvidia CEO shock compounds Fed-hike selloff
items.summary: Bitcoin fell as low as $71,262 intraday Thursday (-3.5%) before settling near $71.4k, extending Tuesday's post-CPI crash; the Alternative.me crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 28 (Fear) as of this run, down slightly from 29 the prior day, after touching extreme-fear territory (25) earlier in the week -- its first sub-30 reading since August.
items.actionable: Crypto is now moving in lockstep with the gold/silver/miner drawdown and the broader risk-off from the Nvidia CEO shock -- a cross-check that this is a market-wide deleveraging into the Dec FOMC rather than an idiosyncratic metals move, reinforcing a defensive stance across all the levered/long-duration sleeves of the book.

items.headline: Today's catalysts: US Core PPI (21:30 SGT) and China October M2/New Loans (18:03 SGT) still ahead
items.summary: US Core PPI m/m is forecast at +0.3% (prior +0.7%) and headline PPI at +0.4% (prior +1.3%), the first major data point since Tuesday's hot CPI and due at 21:30 SGT. China's M2 money-supply y/y is forecast flat at 7.2% while new yuan loans are forecast to plunge to RMB 80B from RMB 1,080B prior (both due 18:03 SGT) -- a normal seasonal air-pocket after October's tax-payment drain, not itself a stress signal.
items.actionable: A Core PPI print at or above forecast would reinforce the Dec-hike repricing and extend pressure on the silver/miner book and SGX bank/REIT discount-rate sensitivity, while a soft miss would be the first disinflation data point in over a week and a plausible relief-rally trigger -- size any pre-print moves in GDX/SLV/REITs conservatively given the binary setup.

items.headline: Fed's Waller floats a half-point December hike after hot CPI confirms his trigger condition
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the Fed should hike in December and warned that hiking only 25bp would put Fed credibility at risk if core CPI printed at or above 0.3% m/m -- which it then did (core +0.3%, headline +0.4%). Markets moved from pricing a possible hold to roughly 88-95% odds of a 25bp hike and ~12-14% odds of a 50bp hike at the Dec 8-9 FOMC.
items.actionable: The hawkish December hike remains the single biggest standing headwind to the silver/gold-miners book and the SGX REIT/bank discount-rate outlook -- the Dec 8-9 FOMC is now the key resolution date for the 50bp tail risk and should anchor position sizing across the levered silver, miners, and REIT sleeves until then.

items.headline: Taiwan Strait tension rises: two PLA carrier groups at sea simultaneously, record aircraft incursions
items.summary: Taiwan counted 49 PLA aircraft crossing on Nov 2, the most of any day in 2026, while both the Liaoning (Philippine Sea) and Fujian (South China Sea) carrier groups were at sea at once in what analysts call drills simulating isolation of Taiwan; Defense Minister Wellington Koo confirmed the 'area denial' exercises on Nov 10. Taiwan holds mayoral elections late November and a stalled $14B US arms package remains unresolved.
items.actionable: Elevated but not yet war-footing Taiwan Strait risk is a standing tail-risk discount on the HK tech book (Tencent, Xiaomi, SMIC), now compounded by the Nvidia leadership vacuum's chip-policy uncertainty -- monitor into Taiwan's late-November mayoral elections for an escalation trigger.

items.headline: Singapore bank Q3 earnings split: OCBC beats, DBS and UOB miss; all three stocks fell on results week
items.summary: OCBC net profit rose 3.2% y/y to S$2.04B (beating estimates), while DBS profit fell ~5% to S$2.81B (markets trading income -65%) and UOB also missed; DBS shares fell toward S$69-71 and OCBC slipped as investors turned cautious on the earnings outlook.
items.actionable: Weak trading-income trends and a cautious market reaction to DBS/UOB misses argue for trimming/hedging the SGX bank exposure (DBS, OCBC) rather than adding into results-week weakness, with OCBC the relative-strength pick of the three -- a read-through that is now reinforced by today's hawkish-Fed-driven discount-rate pressure.

items.headline: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding books $6.98B in new orders YTD, beating full-year target by 55%
items.summary: Yangzijiang Shipbuilding secured $6.98B in new orders in the first ten months of 2026 versus a $4.5B full-year target, with an outstanding orderbook of $26.3B through 2030; roughly two-thirds of contract value is clean-energy newbuildings. Seatrium and YZJ shares climbed after the business update.
items.actionable: Strong, well-above-target order intake is a clean positive for the YZJ shipbuilding position and supportive-by-association for Seatrium; the orderbook visibility through 2030 de-risks the thesis against the macro noise elsewhere in the book.

items.headline: Barrick files IPO for new North American entity 'American Barrick Gold Corp' (NYSE: ABGC)
items.summary: Barrick Mining filed to IPO a new company holding its North American gold assets (to list as ABGC on NYSE), alongside better-than-expected Q3 results; this follows an August deal where Newmont will pay Barrick ~$2B to fold Fourmile and other Nevada properties into their joint venture (61.5%/38.5% split preserved).
items.actionable: A direct corporate-action catalyst for the GOLD/Barrick position -- the spin-off/IPO structure could unlock value but also adds near-term execution/overhang risk on top of the broader gold-miner drawdown; worth tracking the IPO filing details as they firm up.

items.headline: MP Materials: Goldman cuts price target to $57 despite Q3 beat; stock still down ~53% from 52-week high
items.summary: MP Materials reported a surprise adjusted profit on Nov 5 with rare-earth output up 41% y/y and sharply higher sales, driven by GM magnet qualification and future Apple demand, but shares fell 11.9% in October and Goldman trimmed its target from $65 to $57 (kept Buy).
items.actionable: Fundamentals (output, GM/Apple offtake) are improving even as the stock de-rates on valuation -- now that the Nov 10 export-control deadline has resolved favorably (extended to Jan 10, 2027), this is a cleaner re-entry point to revisit on the rare-earth watchlist.
